paragraphs: The London Digital Humanities Seminars are a joint initiative between the [King's College London Computational Humanities Research Group](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/research/computational-humanities-research-group), and the [University College London Centre for Digital Humanities](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/digital-humanities/), founded on an acknowledgement that the field is united by a shared set of methodological considerations, rather than a unitary object of study.

Medievalists, historians, literary scholars, and social scientists working within DH all arrive with different questions, but increasingly make use of similar tools. How a model was built, where a tool broke down, and what theoretical questions an approach raised are questions that are relevant to every DH practitioner, regardless of their disciplinary background. The LDHS is therefore built on the premise that methodology is not a narrow technical concern but the shared language that can form the basis of a genuinely interdisciplinary DH community.
